title: Universality in the target arrival statistics of non-conservative search processes
authors: José Giral-Barajas, Samantha Linn, Paul C. Bressloff
abstract: Stochastic search processes in which searchers are continuously introduced to and removed from a target search domain are fundamental to a wide class of physical and artificial systems. The theory of such non-conservative search processes is, however, much less developed than for search processes with a fixed number of particles. Here we exploit a natural mapping between non-conservative stochastic search and queueing theory to derive the full time-dependent distribution of target arrivals under minimal assumptions on the underlying search process. Remarkably, we find that the steady-state inter-arrival time distribution is exactly exponential, regardless of the details of the search process, showing a robust universality that emerges directly from the queueing framework. Thus, counterintuitively, the arrival statistics of a non-conservative search process are much simpler than sequential search-and-capture processes involving a fixed number of searchers. This has major implications for target resource accumulation, where the delivery of resources is counter-balanced by their downstream consumption.
summary: This paper develops a queueing theory framework to analyze stochastic search processes where resources are continuously added and lost. By mapping the problem to an M_t/G/infinity queue, the authors prove that the steady-state arrival statistics of targets are universally governed by an exponential distribution. This result significantly simplifies the theoretical description of resource accumulation in non-conservative physical systems.
main_problem: Analyzing target arrival statistics for non-conservative stochastic search processes where searchers are continuously introduced and removed from a domain.
main_result: The steady-state inter-arrival time distribution for these non-conservative search processes is exactly exponential, demonstrating robust universality regardless of the underlying search process details.
method: The authors map the non-conservative stochastic search problem onto an M_t/G/infinity queueing system to derive the full time-dependent arrival distributions.
model_or_system: The model involves a target resource accumulation scenario where searchers are subject to continuous introduction (Poisson process) and removal (mortality). This is mathematically treated as an M_t/G/infinity queue, simplifying analysis compared to fixed-particle systems.
key_observables: Target arrival intensity function ($\lambda_\lambda(t)$), steady-state inter-arrival time density ($	ext{f}_{\Delta}(t)$), and the probability of finding the target before mortality ($p_\mu$).
important_parameters: Insertion rate ($\lambda$), mortality rate ($\mu$), and the First Passage Time (FPT) distribution characterizing single-searcher dynamics.
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily assumes homogeneous Poisson insertion of searchers ($\lambda(t) \equiv \lambda > 0$) to establish the universal exponential result. The framework relies on mapping to an M/G/infinity queue.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process mapped onto an M_t/G/infinity queue and show the convergence of the target arrival intensity function to a steady-state rate ($\lambda p_\mu$) for various physical search models.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general queueing theory results (M/G/infinity) to apply these tools specifically to non-conservative search processes. It establishes the mapping, derives the time-dependent arrival statistics, and culminates in proving the universal exponential nature of the steady-state inter-arrival times.
why_interesting: The finding of universal exponential statistics from a complex physical process (search/resource accumulation) is highly relevant to open quantum systems where environmental coupling often leads to Markovian or Poissonian decay rates, simplifying otherwise intractable dynamics.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

(a) Example sample paths of a non-conservative 1D Brownian motion search with ex- ponential insertion and mortality of rates λ = µ = 1. (b) Departures correspond either to target hits (S = T , blue tri- angles) or mortality events (S = M, red crosses). This pro- cess is precisely the departure process of an Mt/G/∞queue. (c) Searchers are continuously inserted into the queue (Ω) ac- cording to a nonhomogeneous Poisson process of rate λ(t). They remain there for a random time S = min{T , M} before departing the system.
